Welcome—I'm so glad you're here. Have you ever found yourself bending over backwards for others, always putting their needs ahead of your own, yet somehow feeling empty or overlooked? You're definitely not alone. Together, we're about to explore why patterns of self-sacrifice and chasing approval often leave us feeling unfulfilled, no matter how hard we try to do the right thing.
In Robert A. Glover’s No More Mr. Nice Guy, we get a revealing look behind the mask of the so-called "nice guy"—the one who avoids conflict, craves validation, and quietly wonders why true happiness always seems just out of reach. What’s driving those habits? It’s often deep beliefs about worthiness and love, shaping how we show up in our relationships, our work, and even how we see ourselves.
As we dig deeper, we’ll uncover the roots of these patterns—moving through feelings like shame, fear, and the longing to be accepted. The journey isn’t about becoming cold or uncaring. Instead, it’s about spotting those hidden motivations, learning to set boundaries that actually honor who we are, and discovering the power of authenticity.
Imagine peeling away the layers of people-pleasing and stepping into a space where self-respect, assertiveness, and real connection become possible. That’s what’s waiting for us as we walk this path—not harshness, but a sense of agency and a life that feels true and fulfilling.
So, are you ready to dive in and see what’s really possible when you let go of the old "nice guy" story? Let’s explore this journey together.
